checker_add.name: lean
checker_add.hash_of: sha256 of bin/lean of the elan toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.22.0 (linux/amd64, darwin/arm64)
checker_add.entry: lake build in a scratch copy with every .olean deleted, then `#print axioms GemJoin.Ilk.ilk_correct` (pilot/verifier/tcgverify/checkers.py lean_project)
checker_add.accept_rule: build exit 0, no sorry/admit in the certificate source, axioms within lean_axioms
checker_add.proof_style: kernel evaluation (kernel_theorem: Eq.refl added with addDecl, so only the kernel checks it) and decide +kernel; no native_decide, no Lean.ofReduceBool, no Lean.trustCompiler
checker_add.cost_note: measured on the VM (8 vCPU): GemJoin library 637 s wall, 5.9 GB peak, with Mathlib oleans present. The verifier deletes every .olean including the dependencies', so a verifier run also rebuilds the imported part of Mathlib from source: not measured

assumptions_add.name: Lean kernel soundness (variant B checker)
assumptions_add.note: Lean 4 v4.22.0 kernel; replaces A3 (kprove) for claim-02 under variant B only. The certificate is re-checked from source, so the elaborator and tactics are untrusted; the kernel and the axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound are trusted
assumptions_add.risk_if_false: a kernel bug could accept a false claim-02 statement

assumptions_add.name: EVMYulLean adequacy for the claim-02 path
assumptions_add.note: A1 gains a second semantics: the Lean statement is about EVMYulLean 56253eb4, not about mainnet. The ilk() path executes 77 instructions of 53 opcodes all present in EVMYulLean's step; no conformance pass rate was measured here
assumptions_add.risk_if_false: an EVMYulLean rule on the path (CALLDATALOAD, SLOAD, MSTORE, MLOAD, JUMPI, RETURN, ...) that differs from mainnet would make the Lean claim false of the deployed contract; agreement with KEVM on claim-02 (cross_checked) makes a shared error less likely, not impossible

assumptions_add.name: patch 0001: fuel-bounded D_J_aux equals upstream partial D_J_aux
assumptions_add.argument: every recursive call needs i < c.size and advances i by at most 33 without wrapping, so fuel c.size + 1 is never exhausted while c.size + 33 < 2^256. Not provable: a partial def has no equations
assumptions_add.evidence: empirical, not a verdict: compiled #eval of the upstream body (copied verbatim as a partial def) and of patched D_J give the same 59 entries [16, 113, 169, ..., 3354] on the GemJoin runtime, equal to the kernel-checked table (GemJoin.DJ.D_J_runtime) and to an independent Python scan, all stopping at 3470. WETH9/Vat not checked (no runtime bytecode on the VM)
assumptions_add.risk_if_false: JUMP/JUMPI destinations accepted or rejected differently from upstream; a proof could certify a run upstream rejects, or the reverse

assumptions_add.name: patch 0002: ByteArray.zeroes n = ⟨Array.replicate n 0⟩ matches upstream's C memset_zero
assumptions_add.argument: equal for n < 2^64; compiled upstream passes n mod 2^64 beyond that, unreachable under any gas schedule. The extern is removed, so kernel and compiled code agree on the patched tree
assumptions_add.risk_if_false: wrong memory contents or sizes after MSTORE, padded reads or RETURN

assumptions_add.name: Lean dependencies fetched by lake
assumptions_add.note: Mathlib and its dependencies are not in the bundle; lake fetches them at the git revs in hard/certs/ilk/lake-manifest.json (verifier reports them in outside_bundle). They are rebuilt from source by the kernel, so a bad dependency can only add axioms (caught by the whitelist) or break the build
assumptions_add.risk_if_false: a dependency rev could become unavailable and make L1 for claim-02 unreproducible (checker_unavailable / not_accept, never a false accept)
